title: Design System: Dino Shrine '98
scope: The dino pane only (mods/dino/hooks/register.ts). Not a system for the other mods in this repository.

extensions.platform: Claude Code pane drawn from Box, Text and Button primitives; rendered by a terminal and by the Desktop app from one tree. No CSS, fonts, px, shadows or breakpoints. Tokens are hex inks, cell widths in character columns, ASCII glyphs of at most two characters, and borderStyle names.

ground.purpose: Page background and the background of every star, divider and banner cell.

star.purpose: The . and + stars; the far stars on the lane's top row. Outside the web-safe register by the world's choice.

starBright.purpose: The * stars only. Outside the web-safe register by the world's choice.

banner.purpose: DINO block letters, the record notice, the help heading.

bannerDark.purpose: The bottom row of the banner. Outside the web-safe register by the world's choice.

text.purpose: SCORE label, HI readout, counter digits, tagline, warning and paused status.

link.purpose: Controls as links, lit meter segments, invitation status.

border.purpose: The table's double border at rest.

box.purpose: Header cell and counter digit boxes.

white.purpose: The live score value and the counter prose.

muted.purpose: Secondary prose: steps, Esc note, help footnote.

cell.purpose: The lane; glyph ink on dinosaur and cactus cells.

dead.purpose: Dinosaur, table border and status when the run is over.

typographyMeta.note: Not applicable: character-cell pane. The only type properties set are bold and dimColor on Text.

motion.name: step
motion.value: 120 ms at start, 10 ms faster every 100 points, floor 60 ms
motion.purpose: The game clock; one redraw per step. Nothing moves while paused or over.

motion.name: divider-march
motion.purpose: Dividers advance with the score; the three on the page are out of phase (score, score+1, score).

motion.name: ground-scroll
motion.purpose: The 8-step GROUND_TILE grain advances with the score.

motion.name: star-drift
motion.purpose: Star rows and the lane's far stars shift by floor(score / 4); the three rows sample the tile at phase, phase+5, phase+3.

motion.name: leg-alternate
motion.purpose: Legs read |\ on even scores and /\ on odd ones; \/ through a jump.

motion.name: record-blink
motion.purpose: *NEW HIGH SCORE* blinks while the run continues and holds steady once it is over.

motion.name: landing-dust
motion.purpose: .: in dirtLit one column behind the dinosaur on the frame after a jump's last arc step.

breakpoints.name: wide-cells
breakpoints.purpose: Cells are 2 columns wide at or above this and 1 below; the picture is 60 or 30 columns across.

breakpoints.name: auto-help
breakpoints.purpose: The FAQ section opens on a fresh game at or above this width.

breakpoints.name: pane-rows
breakpoints.purpose: The rows the pane requests from ui.open.

platformConstraints: The Desktop collapses whitespace: alignment comes from Box width and backgroundColor, never from padded text or leading spaces.
The Desktop draws non-ASCII glyphs in a wider fallback face: cell glyphs are ASCII, at most cw characters.
The Desktop draws a Button's hotkey as a key badge: the terminal's [ ] brackets around links become a | separator there.
Theme colour keys and hex both work on the Desktop; this world uses hex only.

narrative.overview:
The pane is a 1998 single-subject fan page devoted to the dinosaur, and the game is the shrine's centrepiece. The page is a star-tiled navy ground; the name DINO sits at the top in hot-pink block letters; the lane runs inside a centred, double-bordered table; marching ~ dividers separate every section; and the bottom carries a hit counter that is really your games played. It refuses the category default of a bare lane with a status line above it.

This is not a web page. The surface is a Claude Code pane drawn from Box, Text and Button primitives, rendered by a terminal and by the Desktop app from the same tree. Every "pixel" is a fixed-width Box with a backgroundColor and at most two ASCII characters. There are no fonts, px sizes, shadows or breakpoints; the tokens are hex inks, cell widths in character columns, ASCII glyphs and borderStyle names.
keyCharacteristics: Navy star-tiled ground behind everything; the page never shows bare terminal background.
A palette of saturated inks on dark ground: pink banner, yellow labels, cyan links, lime dinosaur, orange cacti.
Every element is a row of fixed-width cells; alignment comes from cell widths and colour, never from padded text.
The page moves on the game clock: dividers march, stars drift, the record notice blinks, the legs alternate.
Each state (fresh, running, paused, over, record) reads from colour alone, without reading a sentence.

rules.name: The Lit Number Rule
rules.body: In the header the label is yellow and the live score is white: the value that changes every step is always the brightest ink in its row.

rules.name: The Crash Ink Rule
rules.body: Game over is told by colour before text: the dinosaur's background and the table border both switch from their rest inks to dead. No other state recolours the border.

rules.name: The Register Rule
rules.body: The palette reads as the 216-colour web-safe register; three inks sit just outside it where the register had no close value (`star`, `starBright`, `bannerDark`). A new ink should read as web-safe to the eye.

rules.name: The Two-Glyph Rule
rules.body: A cell carries at most cw ASCII characters and never a leading space. Alignment comes from the Box width and its background, because the Desktop collapses whitespace and widens non-ASCII glyphs.

dos: Do draw every picture element as a fixed-width Box with a background and at most cw ASCII characters, so the terminal and the Desktop draw the same cells.
Do keep the page 30 cells wide and size cells by bodyColumns >= 62, so the banner and table stay centred in both widths.
Do tell state by ink first: cyan for an invitation, yellow for a warning or pause, red for a crash, pink for a record.
Do put the brackets around links only in the terminal; on the Desktop the hotkey badge is the chrome and a | separates the links.
Do move only on the clock: dividers, ground, stars, legs and the blink all follow the score, never a timer of their own.
donts: Don't align with padded text or leading spaces; the Desktop collapses whitespace.
Don't use non-ASCII or symbol glyphs in cells; the Desktop draws them in a wider face and the picture breaks.
Don't add an ink that does not read as web-safe; the three off-register inks are the world's own and not a licence for more.
Don't recolour the table border for any state other than game over.
Don't carry any of this into another mod; the other games use theme colour keys and their own grammar.
